script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a form read, not a market script, and neither side is assumed to blow the other out. Cincinnati has been a Chase Brown carry game (36 carries, 136 rush yards in two games) plus Tee Higgins downfield (16 targets, 154 yards, 210 air yards), against a Pittsburgh defense allowing 4.54 YPC, 7 runs of 10+, and outside YPA of 9.1 left / 8.53 right. Pittsburgh, already without Rico Dowdle (15 carries, 7 targets) and guard Gennings Dunker, has been inefficient throwing (DK Metcalf 19 targets, 67 yards on 266 air yards; Aaron Rodgers EPA/db -0.42 with no blitz and -0.36 vs blitz) and more of a dink offense through Jaylen Warren (10 targets, 61 yards, negative air) and Pat Freiermuth (10 targets, 78 yards) if Warren plays.
script.flip1: Pittsburgh blitzes at its 25% rate and Cincinnati's split shows up: EPA/db -0.62 vs blitz against +0.27 with no blitz. Joe Burrow's deep shots stall, Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase yards die, quick throws to Brown, Mike Gesicki and Samaje Perine rise, and Cincinnati rush efficiency falls with the pressure.
script.flip2: Jaylen Warren (questionable, shoulder) is inactive or snap-limited on top of Dowdle already out. Pittsburgh has no credible run game (Kenneth Gainwell is not in the log; Trey Homer 2 carries, Gunner Bernard is a receiver, Lew Nichols has no games), falls behind, and throws. Metcalf, Roman Wilson and Freiermuth volume spike; if Cincinnati then leads late, Brown's carries rise and Higgins can stall after a fast start.

injury_fallout: Andrei Iosivas is Out (thumb) after only 4 targets and 19 yards, a small bump toward Higgins (already 8 targets/game), Chase (6.5), Gesicki (3.5), Drew Sample (3 targets, 19 yards) and Erick All (5 rec yards, not in the target log), not a role change. B.J. Hill is Doubtful (Achilles), so Cincinnati's interior run defense is thinner, a modest help to Pittsburgh's run that does not offset Dunker being out. Rico Dowdle is Out (toe), vacating 15 carries/37 yards and 7 targets/28 yards; the next man is Warren only if he plays, and Warren's rush line has no two-sided price so a sleeper move cannot be verified. Gennings Dunker is Out (knee): Pittsburgh pressure should rise, rush efficiency fall, quick throws to Warren/Freiermuth/Bernard rise, and deep Metcalf/Wilson yards get worse. Jamel Dean and Joey Porter Jr. are both Questionable, so Higgins/Chase facing backups is upside, not a confirmed fact; inactives are not in the pack. Michael Pittman is Questionable (foot) and is not in the week 1-2 target log, so his absence may already be the baseline; if he sits, leftover targets tilt to Metcalf and Wilson. Warren Questionable blocks any Pittsburgh RB over until inactives.

matchup.pressure: Pittsburgh blitzes 25% and Cincinnati is a blitz problem (EPA/db -0.62 vs blitz, +0.27 vs none), which kills deep Higgins/Chase yards and pushes checkdowns. Cincinnati blitzes only 11%, and Pittsburgh is slightly negative either way (-0.36 vs blitz, -0.42 vs none), so the Rodgers issue is not blitz-specific. Dunker's absence is the Pittsburgh protection problem that should still raise pressure and cut deep-shot timing.

matchup.overlap: Higgins is Cincinnati's primary (16 targets, 210 air yards, ahead of Chase's 13 targets and 115 air) and that downfield role overlaps Pittsburgh's outside bleed, not the clamped middle. Brown's 36 carries overlap Pittsburgh's 4.54 YPC and explosive-run allowance, but his receiving (11 targets, 24 yards, -27 air) runs into the middle clamp. Gesicki (7 targets, 78 yards, 63 air) also works the area Pittsburgh has clamped. Metcalf's 266 air yards are the deep shots a Cincinnati defense has not bled (7/90 explosives; best split is right side 5.11), and Dunker out makes those shots less likely to connect. Freiermuth and Warren receiving overlap Cincinnati's soft middle, but Freiermuth is 46 and 32 vs 37.5 and Warren is questionable.

form: Two games only, despite L3 labels. Higgins 59 and 95, both over 54.5, with the target and air-yard lead. Chase 12 and 75, both under 77, volatile, and behind Higgins. Brown rush 56 and 80 (one miss of 63.5) on 18 carries/game at 3.78 YPC; receiving 22 and 2. Gesicki last4 shows a single 78, matching the two-game total of 78 yards on 7 targets, so treat it as a spike not a trend. Perine rec 30 and 16, rush 20 and 6, a change-of-pace not a feature. Metcalf 40 and 27, both under 52.5, on 19 targets and 266 air yards: volume without efficiency. Wilson 26 and 28, both barely over 23, on 12 targets, 54 yards and 147 air, and no two-sided price. Freiermuth 46 and 32, a split at 37.5. Warren rush 46 and 43, both under 58; rec 27 and 34, both over 26.5; rush+rec 73 and 77, both under 88; all of it in a committee that no longer includes Dowdle, and all of it health-dependent. Rodgers 1 carry for 5 yards. Burrow 4 carries for 21 yards, likely one spike against a 5.5 line.

pre_mortem: Monday both leans lost. Higgins finished under 54.5 because Pittsburgh blitzed, Cincinnati's -0.62 EPA/db vs blitz showed up, and the outside YPA bleed (20 and 17 attempts, two games) was noise; Dean and Porter played and took away the primary, and a second-half Brown clock-kill (36-carry role) stalled the routes after a quiet first half. Metcalf cleared 52.5 because 266 air yards were a leading indicator, not a fade: one 40-yard completion plus his usual 30 underneath, with Warren inactive so target share jumped, and a questionable corner out so Cincinnati's 7/90 explosive rate did not travel. The counters are close to as strong as the reads, which is why both stay leans and flagged, not strong and not sized.
slip_story: One story only: Cincinnati's downfield WR wins outside against a Pittsburgh defense that bleeds left and right, while Pittsburgh's own downfield game stays broken with Dunker out. That is a Higgins over plus Metcalf under pair, not a shootout stack and not a favorite-runs-the-clock stack. Do not add Brown rush over on the same slip: that leg needs Cincinnati to grind the clock, which can stall Higgins, and 56 already missed 63.5. Do not add Freiermuth or Warren overs: they need Pittsburgh to complete the intermediate throws that can ride with a Metcalf explosive. No TD legs, one market per player, and no bet is placed. Warren, Pittman, Dean and Porter are game-time decisions; rerun before inactives.
